note: Presets are saved parameter sets for the same animation; they do not count as additional animations. Components, labels and relationships are generic, fictional and supplied by the author; lines are plain relations, a communication and a numbered sequence captioned as configured — no arrows. 'Archived' is only another shelf block in this example; nothing states a retention period, an access or destruction rule, a time span or any outcome. Coordinator decision (standing rule 2026-09-26, AUTHORING item 20; from LAW-0687/0689–0692): long-labels-stress is capped. The true drivers, measured by the independent review (courts-09, 2026-09-27) on the rendered near-maximum values (7 component labels of 42–49 characters, 7–8 relationship labels of 45–50 characters): rendered text itself stays >= 16 px in every ratio, but (1) relationship labels are ellipsised — one at 9:16 and two at 1:1 (the console-to-block lines) — which AUTHORING item 2 forbids; (2) with all seven component labels the clerk drops to 59.6 px at 1:1, below the 60 px floor; (3) with eight relationships the identifier, file and block chips cannot be placed (chip-place-* problems). Fallbacks tried first: a right-hand text column (plan scale 0.47, clerk 47 px < 60), larger top margins for the block chips (80/105/130 template units), a vertical spread of the lower components in portrait, narrower chip widths (340/250/190 px) and narrower label wraps (1–3 lines). Capped values (the longest found to fit every ratio with no ellipsis): three component labels of 34–36 characters (baseline 13–30), six relationships (baseline count 6) with labels of 28–33 characters (baseline 14–22); every other field stays at near-maximum length (courts, routes, seats, labels, identifier, relation-kind captions, eight traversal steps). Rendered result with the capped values (probe and tests, 2026-09-27): 1:1 text 16.6 px, clerk 60.9 px; 9:16 text 18.9 px, clerk 73.1 px; 16:9 text 19.8 px, clerk 86.1 px.
